title: Virtual Press Conference RE BAAJA
content:
Jordan Harmon, policy analyst and legislative advocate at the Indigenous Environmental Network. Growing up in the oil and gas hub of Tulsa, Oklahoma, once dubbed the “Oil and Gas Capital of the World,” Jordan witnessed firsthand the negative environmental and economic impacts of the fossil fuels industry and currently focuses on influencing public policy that will benefit Indigenous peoples, open spaces, and the environment while ensuring Tribal sovereignty and free, prior and informed consent is upheld.

Rashida Tlaib, member of Congress, U.S. House of Representatives. Democratic Representative Tlaib has served the people of Michigan since 2019 representing the 12th Congressional district. As a lawyer and the first Palestinian American woman to serve in Congress she has consistently supported environmental and economic policies that prioritize community health and well-being, especially in the face of corporate interests. She sits on the House Environmental Justice Caucus that she founded with Representatives Summer L. Lee (PA-12) and Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07).

Daisy Maldonado, organizer with Fight Chihuahuan Desert Xtraction in New Mexico. Daisy is a trained economist and has been a community organizer in the area for twenty years. title: Indigenous Just Transition in The Arctic
content:
This is going to be a collaborative event between Ungeirr Umkveraasenaar, or the Icelandic Young Environmentalists, and the Indigenous Environmental Network. Maybe we can go around and you guys can give a little introduction about yourselves. Sure.

Huang’a a’ka, pang’a’anang naka pang’a’u yu, huang’a a’taka, a’anatirma, naka kirstinuga pás, huang’a sivunga rumi. I come from St. Lawrence Island. I’ve been with IEN since 2021, and I work on organizing against climate geoengineering.

Kweyanaipaplusi maunga, huang’a a’akaluk, ungelaksirmiu runga, angayukang maktaklu Charlie. I a’anukwa’apu’a makigaklu anaktiyuk asii, janililu Charlie, chinirmiu, ungelaksirmiu. Thank you everyone for welcoming us here today.

I’m Adrienne A’akaluk Blatchford. I’m from Unalakleet, Alaska, which is up on the Northwest Coast in the passageway to the Arctic. We’re right on the coast of the Bering Sea in the heart of the Norton Sound.

And I work with Indigenous Environmental Network as a geoengineering outreach organizer with a focus on Alaska and the Arctic. Hello, thank you for having us as the host.

My name is Thomas Joseph. I’m a Hoopa Valley tribal member from the Six Rivers National Forest in Northern California. I am also Shoshone Paiute from the Sierra Nevadas. Paiute is what we call it, the land of flowing water.
